headline: IBM introduced a new way of running programs on its quantum computers that lets researchers see and adjust how errors are handled.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 2: IBM's post is dated 5 Oct and the item was already in our 6 Oct pool; it is a developer tool described by IBM itself.
importance_line: Researchers who study quantum error handling get more visibility and control on IBM's machines, but it is a tool for specialists, the benefits are IBM's own account, and the news is five days old.
summary: IBM says in a blog post dated 5 Oct 2026, summarised by Quantum Computing Report on 10 Oct, that its new directed execution model moves the error-reduction steps that used to run hidden on IBM's servers onto the researcher's own side, where they can be inspected and changed. It rests on a new tool called Executor, and IBM says users of its standard Sampler and Estimator tools can keep their existing code.
notes: Read IBM's own blog post (original) and Quantum Computing Report's summary; the link is IBM's post. Pool item C15-09 of 6 Oct covered the IBM post as pool only. Category MOD (tool) from default RES.
